CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Padang Pariaman Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Padang Pariaman Regency. 4. Regional Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is a Regional Work Unit within the Government of Padang Pariaman Regency. 5. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improvement of quality of life, and enhancement of women's participation in development. 6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and is not married. 8. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 11. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development policies, programs and activities. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 19. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore mental health through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 30.

Article 68
The family in efforts to Protect the rights of women has the role to:
a. protect women from conflict and Violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities to women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. prevent the occurrence of violations against the rights of women in the household.

Article 21
(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women can be made by reporters consisting of:
a. victims,
b. family,
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of Protection of Women and Children, such as: P2TP2A, Safe Houses, etc.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may file complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of Violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by the Regent's Regulation.

Article 27
(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in handling cases of Violence against women, particularly to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.
(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

Article 30
(1) Social reintegration is carried out in the context of reuniting women victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
(2) Social reintegration is aimed so that:
a. women victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and
b. women victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

Article 25
(1) The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of Violence.
(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women victims of acts of Violence who require safe houses include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services shall be regulated by a Regent's Regulation.

CHAPTER IX
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 70
(1) The Local Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
 a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
 b. technical guidance and training;
 c. provision of facilities;
 d. monitoring; and
 e. evaluation.
(3) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence in accordance with minimum service standards.

Article 23
(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter c is intended to restore and develop the capabilities of women victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by:
a. SKPD that has duties and functions in the social field;
b. SKPD that oversees Women's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centres or existing social community organizations; or
c. the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

Part Two
Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women

CHAPTER III
PROTECTION OF WOMEN
Part One
General

Article 31
The Regional Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of women victims of acts of Violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 29
(1) Repatriation is intended to return women victims of acts of Violence to their Region of origin.
(2) Repatriation of women victims of acts of Violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

Article 48
(1) Regional Governments are obligated to provide comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the time they are in the womb.
(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
   a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
   b. exemption from cost burdens for malnourished Children, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children who are victims of abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, Children who become victims of Violence, and Children who are victims of human trafficking; and
(3) Regional Governments, communities, families and parents are obligated to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 46
(1) Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
(2) Every Child has the right to obtain Protection in educational units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

Article 46
(1) Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.

CHAPTER IX
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 70
(1) The Local Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
 a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
 b. technical guidance and training;
 c. provision of facilities;
 d. monitoring; and
 e. evaluation.
(3) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence in accordance with minimum service standards.

Article 25
(1) The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of Violence.
(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women victims of acts of Violence who require safe houses include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services shall be regulated by a Regent's Regulation.

Article 30
(1) Social reintegration is carried out in the context of reuniting women victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
(2) Social reintegration is aimed so that:
a. women victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and
b. women victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

Article 65
Service efforts carried out by Regional Governments for child victims of acts of Violence as referred to in Article 42 through Article 64 apply mutatis mutandis to service efforts for Child victims of acts of Violence.

Article 23
(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter c is intended to restore and develop the capabilities of women victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by:
a. SKPD that has duties and functions in the social field;
b. SKPD that oversees Women's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centres or existing social community organizations; or
c. the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women

Article 48
(1) Regional Governments are obligated to provide comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the time they are in the womb.
(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
   a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
   b. exemption from cost burdens for malnourished Children, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children who are victims of abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, Children who become victims of Violence, and Children who are victims of human trafficking; and
(3) Regional Governments, communities, families and parents are obligated to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 21
(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women can be made by reporters consisting of:
a. victims,
b. family,
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of Protection of Women and Children, such as: P2TP2A, Safe Houses, etc.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may file complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of Violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by the Regent's Regulation.

Article 45
(1) Every organizer of an educational unit is obligated to provide opportunities to Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.
(2) Every organizer of an educational unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.
(3) In the event that a Child victim of an act of Violence experiences dropping out of school, the organizer of the educational unit is obligated to coordinate with relevant agencies.

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women can be made by reporters consisting of:
a. victims,
b. family,
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of Protection of Women and Children, such as: P2TP2A, Safe Houses, etc.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may file complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of Violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by the Regent's Regulation.

Article 25
(1) The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of Violence.
(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women victims of acts of Violence who require safe houses include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services shall be regulated by a Regent's Regulation.

Article 30
(1) Social reintegration is carried out in the context of reuniting women victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
(2) Social reintegration is aimed so that:
a. women victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and
b. women victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

Article 23
(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter c is intended to restore and develop the capabilities of women victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by:
a. SKPD that has duties and functions in the social field;
b. SKPD that oversees Women's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centres or existing social community organizations; or
c. the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

Article 68
The family in efforts to Protect the rights of women has the role to:
a. protect women from conflict and Violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities to women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. prevent the occurrence of violations against the rights of women in the household.

Article 66
(1) Community participation in efforts to Protect women and Children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and Children to the competent authorities; and
c. monitor the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and Children.
(2) Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and Children.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is in accordance with statutory regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 31
The Regional Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of women victims of acts of Violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 66
(1) Community participation in efforts to Protect women and Children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children;

CHAPTER IX
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 70
(1) The Local Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
 a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
 b. technical guidance and training;
 c. provision of facilities;
 d. monitoring; and
 e. evaluation.
(3) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence in accordance with minimum service standards.

Article 27
(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in handling cases of Violence against women, particularly to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.
(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

Article 25
(1) The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of Violence.
(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women victims of acts of Violence who require safe houses include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services shall be regulated by a Regent's Regulation.

Article 21
(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women can be made by reporters consisting of:
a. victims,
b. family,
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of Protection of Women and Children, such as: P2TP2A, Safe Houses, etc.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may file complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of Violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by the Regent's Regulation.

Article 40
Communication, information and education as referred to in Article 39 letter a constitutes communication activities to increase knowledge and improve the attitudes and behavior of families and communities in the Population and family planning Program.

Article 23
(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter c is intended to restore and develop the capabilities of women victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by:
a. SKPD that has duties and functions in the social field;
b. SKPD that oversees Women's Empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centres or existing social community organizations; or
c. the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

Article 30
(1) Social reintegration is carried out in the context of reuniting women victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
(2) Social reintegration is aimed so that:
a. women victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and
b. women victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

Third Part
Effectiveness of Services for Women Victims of Acts of Violence

Article 46
(1) Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
(2) Every Child has the right to obtain Protection in educational units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

Article 21
(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women can be made by reporters consisting of:

b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services shall be regulated by a Regent's Regulation.

Article 23
(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter c is intended to restore and develop the capabilities of women victims of acts of Violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improvement of quality of life, and enhancement of women's participation in development. 6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and is not married. 8. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development policies, programs and activities. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 19. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. 21. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore mental health through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 30.

Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 19. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore mental health through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 30.

Article 66
(1) Community participation in efforts to Protect women and Children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and Children to the competent authorities; and
c. monitor the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and Children.
(2) Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and Children.

(4) Further provisions regarding the establishment of the Children’s Forum as referred to in paragraphs (1) through (3) shall be stipulated by a Regent Decree.

Article 25

b. provision of safe houses; and

d. all work that endangers the health, safety, or morals of Children.

Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improvement of quality of life, and enhancement of women's participation in development. 6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and is not married. 8. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 11. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development policies, programs and activities. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 19. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Article 25

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women victims of acts of Violence who require safe houses include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.

Part Two
Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women

Article 21
(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women can be made by reporters consisting of:
a. victims,
b. family,
c. community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of Protection of Women and Children, such as: P2TP2A, Safe Houses, etc.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may file complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of Violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by the Regent's Regulation.

Article 30
(1) Social reintegration is carried out in the context of reuniting women victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
(2) Social reintegration is aimed so that:
a. women victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and
b. women victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

Article 27
(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in handling cases of Violence against women, particularly to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.
(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

Fourth Part
Health and Social

Article 66
(1) Community participation in efforts to Protect women and Children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and Children to the competent authorities; and
c. monitor the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and Children.
(2) Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and Children.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is in accordance with statutory regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 32
(1) Employers who employ women are obligated to maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace.
(2) Employers are obligated to place female workers in places that are safe for women's reproductive health.
(3) Employers are obligated to fulfill the rights of female workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) Employers are obligated to provide special breastfeeding facilities at their company.

CHAPTER V
IMPROVEMENT OF FAMILY QUALITY
Article 34
(1) In order to improve family quality, the Regional Government is responsible for:
a. conducting efforts to improve family quality to realize gender equality and the rights of Children;
b. providing services for families in realizing gender equality and the rights of Children;
c. strengthening and developing institutions providing family quality improvement services in the Region; and
(2) The responsibility of the Regional Government in efforts to improve family quality as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by SKPD in accordance with their duties and functions.

Article 57
(1) Every person/entity is prohibited from employing and involving Children in the worst forms of work.

d. all work that endangers the health, safety, or morals of Children.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improvement of quality of life, and enhancement of women's participation in development. 6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and is not married. 8. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 11. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore mental health through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 30.

Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development policies, programs and activities. 13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 19. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore mental health through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. 29. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 30.
